_doc: Alternative question parts the hourly optimizer combines. Index 0 must equal version 1 (jev.V1). The cloud brain (Claude) appends new ideas here; the optimizer only ever promotes what wins on the bench.

instructions: What is a person who types `search_term` into the App Store search box looking for?
Someone typed `search_term` into the App Store search box. Decide what they are trying to find. Use `top_results` only as hints.

instructions.task: Classify the App Store search query `search_term` by what the searcher wants.
instructions.hint: Names of clinics, companies, publishers or specific apps mean they want that one entity; plain topic words mean a need that any good app could serve.

instructions: Decide what the person typing `search_term` wants. If the words identify one particular company, publisher, app, clinic or practice (even when built from ordinary words, or ending in LLC, PC, Inc or a city), they want that one entity. If the words only describe a topic, task, exam or tool that many apps could serve, they want a need. Use `top_results` only as supporting evidence.

criteria.need: A kind of tool, calculator, reference, study aid or utility; any good app doing this job would satisfy them
criteria.brand: One specific company, product, publisher or app, by its name
criteria.local_business: The app of one specific clinic, shop, school, credit union or other organization
criteria.game: A game or simulator to play for fun

criteria.need: Plain words for a topic, task, exam or tool that many apps could serve (e.g. 'welding symbols', 'white noise', 'nclex practice questions'); not a proper name
criteria.brand: A proper name of one product, app, publisher or company, possibly with generic words added (e.g. 'foreflight', 'hinge health', 'pocket prep', 'miller weld setting calculator')
criteria.local_business: Names one specific local clinic, practice, shop, school, hospital or credit union, often with LLC, PC, a city or a person's name
criteria.game: Wants a game, simulator or something to play
criteria.jobs: Wants job listings or to be hired

instructions: Is `search_term` a proper name - the brand, product, company or app name of one specific app or company - rather than plain words describing what the searcher needs? Use `top_results` as evidence: a brand usually appears as the distinctive title of one result.

Would a typical person read `search_term` as the name of one particular product, app, company, publisher, clinic or person, rather than a description of a task or topic? Invented words, trademarks, company or person names, and app titles with taglines are names.

instructions.question: Is `search_term` a name (of one app, product, company, publisher, clinic or person) rather than a description of a need?
instructions.evidence: Check `top_results`: if one result's title or developer contains the distinctive words of `search_term`, it is probably that result's name. If many results share the words, they are probably generic.

instructions: Does `search_term` identify one specific named product, app, company, publisher, publication or person? A name can be built from ordinary words (like 'Paramedic Coach', 'Hinge Health', 'Pharmacy Technician Letter'); a description of a topic, exam or tool is not a name. Use `top_results` only as supporting evidence: many results with similar titles means generic words, one distinctive title or publisher means a name.

criteria.true: A proper or brand name (like 'ForeFlight', 'PassRun', 'Smart Optometry'), possibly with generic words added
criteria.false: Plain descriptive words for a need or topic, even if one app happens to use these words as its title (like 'paramedic exam prep', 'welding symbols', 'acupuncture tools')

criteria.true: It names one specific product, company, app, clinic or person: invented or trademarked words (PassRun, ForeFlight), company or person names (Miller, Hinge Health, Niveta), or an exact app title carrying a tagline or punctuation
criteria.false: Ordinary words describing a topic, task, exam or tool that many apps could serve (paramedic exam prep, welding symbols, white noise), even if one app uses them as its title

criteria.true: Identifies one specific named product, company, publication, publisher or person, even when it is made of ordinary words or ends with a generic word (Paramedic Coach, Hinge Health, Pharmacy Technician Letter, Tinozzi Chiropractic & Massage)
criteria.false: A generic description of a topic, exam, certification or tool, including exam-prep style titles with an acronym, year or 'prep/test/flashcards' (cmtbc massage therapy prep, student midwife baby catches, welding test, hvac flashcards)

instructions: Does `top_results[{i}]` directly serve what a person searching `search_term` wants?
Is `top_results[{i}]` built mainly for the need expressed by `search_term`, so that a searcher would pick it to solve exactly that need?

criteria.true: Built for this need: a real competitor
criteria.false: Unrelated, only loosely related, or a general app that merely mentions it

criteria.true: Its main purpose matches the search need, or it has a full dedicated feature for it
criteria.false: Its main purpose is something else in the same field, a broader topic that only touches the need, an exam or course that only includes some questions on it, or unrelated

instructions: Would {subject} likely be restricted by App Store review because of what the app itself does?
Would Apple's App Review likely reject or restrict {subject} because of what it actually does (not because of its topic)?

criteria.true: The app itself would do something App Review restricts: calculate drug doses for real patients, diagnose or treat medical conditions, give regulated financial or legal advice, run real-money gambling, distribute copyrighted material, or operate a service that needs an official licence
criteria.false: An ordinary app. Study aids, exam prep, flashcards, reference guides, calculators for trades and educational content ABOUT medicine, law or finance are ordinary apps

true.definition: The app performs a restricted activity itself
restricted activities: dosing or treatment advice for real patients
diagnosing conditions or claiming to measure vital signs with phone sensors
regulated financial services, lending, trading with user money, or legal advice
streaming or distributing copyrighted content without rights

examples: study aids, exam prep and flashcards about medicine, law or finance
reminders and trackers that do not give medical decisions

instructions: Who is {subject} built for?
How specialised is the audience of {subject}?
criteria: The general public; anyone could need it
A broad hobby or interest group
People in a specific occupation or trade, or students training for one
A narrow specialty inside an occupation
Anyone: a mass-market everyday need
Hobbyists or a broad interest community
Workers in one occupation or trade, or students preparing for its licence or exam
Specialists inside an occupation (a sub-specialty, certification or niche technique)

instructions: How willing is the target audience of {subject} to pay for it?
If {subject} were excellent, how would its typical user pay for it?
criteria: Expects it to be free; would not pay
Might pay a small one-time amount
Would pay a recurring subscription because it helps their work, income or an exam they must pass
Would not pay; plenty of free alternatives and low stakes
A small one-time purchase at most
A subscription is easy to justify: it saves work time, earns money or helps pass a costly exam

instructions: How feasible is it for one iOS developer to build a high-quality version of {subject} within about four weeks?
Could a single iOS developer ship a competitive version of {subject} in about four weeks?
criteria: Not feasible: needs licensed data, special hardware, partnerships, a big content team or a regulated service
Hard: needs a lot of expert content or complex engineering
Feasible: moderate content or engineering that one developer can produce or source
Easy: mostly interface over public knowledge, formulas or the phone's own sensors
No: requires a marketplace, network effects, licences, hardware or a large team
Barely: a large body of expert content or heavy engineering
Yes, with focused effort: moderate content or engineering
Easily: a simple interface over public facts, formulas or phone sensors

instructions: What kind of app is `app`?
Which category best describes what `app` mainly is?

criteria.utility: A tool that does one job with the phone's sensors, camera, audio, files or calculations
criteria.reference: Reference, learning, study or exam-prep content for a topic
criteria.content: Media, entertainment, streaming, social or news
criteria.ai_wrapper: Mainly a chat or AI-generation interface
criteria.service: Front end for a business, account or online service

criteria.utility: A single-purpose tool (scanner, meter, timer, tracker, converter, identifier, reminder) that works on the device
criteria.reference: Organised knowledge to look up or learn: guides, atlases, drug references, exam-prep question banks
criteria.content: Media to consume: video, music, radio, books, comics, daily verses, social feeds or news
criteria.ai_wrapper: Its core is chatting with or generating text, images or playlists with AI
criteria.service: The app of a company, bank, employer benefit, marketplace or online account the user signs into

instructions: A user rejected an app idea and wrote `note` (Turkish). Which listed reason does the note express?
Bir kullanıcı bir app fikrini reddetti ve `note` notunu yazdı. Not, listedeki hangi sebebi ifade ediyor?

criteria.Alakasız: The app or idea is unrelated to what the user is looking for
criteria.Çok rekabet / doygun: The market niche already has strong, established competitors
criteria.Yapması zor: Too hard or expensive for the user to build
criteria.Para yapmaz: Users would not pay; it would not make money
criteria.Kalitesiz / eski: This particular app listing is low quality or outdated
criteria.Çok benzer: The user keeps seeing too many near-identical apps in this list; it is repetitive
criteria.Ret riski: Likely to be rejected by App Store review
criteria.Sıkıcı fikir: The idea is boring or uninteresting to the user

criteria.Alakasız: Fikir kullanıcının aradığı şeyle ilgisiz (ör. oyun, başka alan)
criteria.Çok rekabet / doygun: Bu nişte zaten güçlü, çok yorumlu rakipler var; pazar doymuş
criteria.Yapması zor: Tek başına yapmak çok zor veya pahalı (sunucu, lisans, içerik ekibi)
criteria.Kalitesiz / eski: Bu app'in kendisi kötü yapılmış veya eski (ikon, ekran görüntüsü, güncelleme)
criteria.Çok benzer: Listede aynısından çok var, tekrar ediyor
